newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine army defector returns in tears.
newsitem.headline: Philippine army defector returns in tears.

text.p: A former Philippine Army general who defected to the communist rebels came down from the mountains in tears on Sunday to help the guerrillas negotiate peace with the government.

Raymundo Jarque, 59, has been given immunity from arrest to allow him to join other Filipino rebels in the Netherlands town of Utrecht, where negotiations between the guerrillas and the Manila government are to resume on March 11.

The communist-led National Democratic Front (NDF), whose leaders live in exile in the Netherlands, has appointed Jarque as its military consultant in the talks aimed at ending a 28-year Marxist insurgency.
"Tears are part of soldiery. Soldiers, too, cry," ex-general Raymundo Jarque told reporters after an emotional reunion with his wife, Xenia, and his son, Rene, himself a captain in the armed forces.
The reunion took place in Bacolod on the central island of Negros where Jarque used to command army forces in the battle against guerrillas of the Communist Party of the Philippines.
Jarque had a machete, not a gun, tucked in his waist when he appeared at a news conference, accompanied by government officials, after a three-day trek from his mountain hideout.
Jarque, who won 30 medals for his exploits against the rebels, had been in retirement for a year when he defected to the guerrillas in October 1995, urging other soldiers to join him.
He switched loyalties after he was charged with various crimes ranging from theft to attempted murder, saying he could not expect justice from a corrupt judicial system.
The charges are still pending in courts in Manila but under an arrangement between government and rebel negotiators, Jarque will be allowed to post bail and go to the Netherlands.
